text: A file at the root of the web bundle other than favicon.svg is swallowed by the SPA fallback — tuppu-cuneiform.svg redirects to login under a prefix mount

Fixed in 883d40d. Web: CuneiformName renders an inline <svg fill=currentColor> with the path (the Android drawable's twin); public svg removed; tests assert an svg with a path and fill currentColor. Server: web_index serves a regular root-level file of web_dist before the SPA fallback (send_from_directory, isfile, no slash), test covers a served file and an unknown name falling through; wire-contract site-root table gained the row. Gate green: server 505, web 419, Android.

Correction to the commit message (history is not rewritten): the "Security error ... may not load or link to file:///" the maintainer saw was their adblocker, not Firefox refusing the mask — with the adblocker off and logged in, the error vanished and the one real fault remained: the SPA fallback answering the svg address with the app page (login page when logged out, front page when logged in), so the mask received HTML and drew nothing. The fix stands unchanged and is stronger for it: an inline path fetches nothing, so no route, no fallback and no content blocker can get between the page and the sign.
